papers.title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription
papers.abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. In this work, we investigate entitylevel analysis of OCR errors as a complementary perspective for evaluating OCR quality in historical documents. Using a publicly available benchmark of 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive, augmented with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that will be released upon acceptance, we compare sequence-recognition OCR systems, OCR-specialized vision-language models, and general-purpose vision-language models. Beyond global transcription accuracy, we analyze entity preservation and recoverability under varying character-level edit tolerances. Our experiments show that OCR rankings depend on the evaluation criterion: while Qwen 3.6 achieves the highest entity coverage across all tested tolerances, several systems with lower exact-match coverage recover substantially when small errors are tolerated, suggesting that many of their errors correspond to localized character-level deviations rather than fundamentally incorrect entity transcriptions. Conversely, some systems remain unable to recover many entities even under relaxed matching. These findings show that OCR quality cannot be fully characterized by aggregate transcription metrics alone and highlight the importance of evaluating how OCR errors affect the preservation and recoverability of meaningful information.

papers.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
papers.abstract: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves $1.45\times$ the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.

papers.title: Fast Path, Exact Path: One Library of Hardwired Operators for Streaming and Exact Canny Edge Detection on a Low-Cost FPGA
papers.abstract: Hysteresis edge tracking, the final stage of Canny edge detection, follows edge chains of unbounded length and therefore resists single-pass streaming; FPGA designs either approximate it or dedicate separate labelling hardware to it. We show that a single library of hardwired 3x3 operators, each with an identical two-clock latency, delivers both a camera-rate approximation and exact hysteresis on a low-cost Artix-7 (XC7A35T). The fast path streams camera pixels through the operators and K local hysteresis stages and commits each edge decision 262.15-720.63 microseconds after the pixel arrives (K = 1-8; system simulation with a datasheet camera model), that is, 3 + K camera lines later and 46-127x sooner than a frame-based processor can even begin at 30 frames per second. It provably never reports an edge that exact hysteresis rejects, recovers 76.6-96.1% of exact edges at thresholds 20/40, and on the 200 BSDS500 test images retains at least 98.6% of the exact path's boundary F-measure (ODS 0.470-0.477 versus 0.476). The exact path holds 128x128 tiles in block RAM, is exact within each tile, and replaces two-buffer iteration with in-place forward and reverse sweeps built into the same operator. This reduces hysteresis from 38-82 passes to 3-7 on pattern and photo tiles, accelerating the hysteresis step 6.6-21.7x (40x on a worst-case tile) and a complete tile 4.5-9.9x, with identical output. Both paths are bit-exact with software golden models at every pipeline stage and close timing at 50 MHz in at most 1455 LUTs. An optimised multi-core CPU remains faster on stored images, but it cannot begin until the frame is complete.

papers.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
papers.abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.

papers.title: DairySocialTwin: Auditing the video-to-graph evidence chain in cattle social networks
papers.abstract: Video-derived social graphs can appear precise while inheriting uncertainty from detection, tracking, classification, and aggregation. We present DairySocialTwin, a graph-centered audit framework applied to 203 videos (122 h 23 min) from 15 views at three commercial dairy farms. Curation retained 447 of 839 candidate clips; 400 entered a frozen source-clip index, including 71 legacy clips with unavailable farm and time metadata. Five models were compared on a development split, with an NRI-style model retained as an exploratory trade-off between class balance and dyadic output. In a 90-min manual audit, reconciliation improved switches, fragmentation, and continuous-track duration across three gap definitions, but constrained identity capacity and inherited detector errors limited claims of identity accuracy. Matched manual and reconciled summaries showed coarse agreement and assignment sensitivity. Camera-specific semantics, observation opportunity, and identity-summary-to-video trace-back made these dependencies inspectable. DairySocialTwin supports auditable relational inference without claiming permanent identity, calibrated behavior, or biological diagnosis.

papers.title: EL-DIP: A Deep Image Prior Framework for Accurate,Efficient, and Noise-Robust Elastography
papers.abstract: Elastography is a key technique for non-invasive imaging, yet it remains severely ill-posed and sensitive to measurement noise, causing blurring and artifacts. We propose EL-DIP, a training-data-free framework based on deep image prior (DIP) that reconstructs heterogeneous shear modulus distributions. Inverse distance weighting interpolation enables arbitrary-shaped domains, and adjoint sensitivity analysis provides efficient gradient computation. Numerical and experimental studies show that EL-DIP accurately recovers inclusion geometry and modulus across different noise levels. Under extreme noise, image fidelity improves by approximately 97.1% over conventional methods. We believe that this method has great potential as a robust tool for biomedical diagnosis,biomechanical characterization, and non-destructive evaluation.

papers.title: Spectrally optimized implicit neural representations mitigate acquisition-related image quality trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI
papers.abstract: 4D Flow MRI promises opportunities for non-invasive mapping of neurovascular hemodynamics, but its clinical utility faces trade-offs between resolution, acquisition time, and noise. Deep learning-based super-resolution offers a post-scan solution, but supervised approaches require paired or domain-specific data, while patient-specific physics-informed models can be computationally demanding. This creates a need for unsupervised reconstruction models that can adapt to individual acquisitions without paired high-resolution training data, while remaining robust across anatomy, disease severity, and acquisition quality. To address this, we introduce a spectrally tuned implicit neural representation (INR) framework for intracranial 4D Flow MRI, representing the velocity field as a continuous coordinate-based neural field using WIRE activation functions with tunable spectral bias. Data-driven and physics-informed variants were evaluated in nine cerebrovascular cases spanning healthy controls and moderate-to-severe intracranial atherosclerotic disease, using CFD-derived high-resolution reference fields, MR-realistic synthetic low-resolution inputs, and direct fitting to acquired in-vivo data. Cohort-optimal spectral-bias settings generalized across subjects with only small increases in relative error compared with subject-specific optima, reducing the need for case-specific hyperparameter tuning. Physics-informed regularization provided modest additional accuracy but required substantially longer optimization, whereas the data-driven INR achieved near-comparable reconstruction performance within minutes. The framework also remained robust to acquisition-realistic noise and moderate VENC-dependent aliasing. These findings establish spectrally optimized INRs as a flexible unsupervised approach for mitigating acquisition-related trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI.

papers.title: Investigating the trackability of landmarks in NBI and WLI
papers.abstract: Reliable visual tracking of anatomical landmarks in endoscopic video is a key prerequisite for computer-assisted interventions in laryngeal surgery. While Narrow Band Imaging (NBI) is clinically established for enhancing vascular contrast, its effect on automated tracking relative to conventional White Light Imaging (WLI) remains unexplored. We present a quantitative comparison of landmark trackability in NBI and WLI using a forward-backward error framework applied to 61 endoscopic videos from 39 patients. Two regions of interest are evaluated: the vocal folds (VF) and mucosa with a prominent vascular pattern (MPVP). We compare a classical feature-based tracker (CSRT) against learning-based point trackers (CoTracker3-Online and TrackOnR) across both modalities. NBI consistently reduced the forward-backward error in both regions, reaching statistical significance for the vocal folds, while failure rates stayed low. These findings indicate that NBI can improve tracking robustness in laryngeal endoscopy, with implications for motion analysis, navigation, and robotic assistance.

papers.title: Beyond Visible Speakers: Context-Aware Active Speaker Detection with Speaker Registration
papers.abstract: Active speaker detection (ASD) relies on audiovisual correspondence between speech and visible faces, yet this correspondence becomes unreliable in crowded scenes, or when visual evidence is unavailable. We introduce ROAM-ASD-C and ROAM-ASD-CR to extend ROAM-ASD with contextual and identity-aware reasoning. ROAM-ASD-C jointly reasons across simultaneously visible candidates, allowing other faces to provide complementary evidence when the target observation is ambiguous or incomplete. ROAM-ASD-CR incorporates registered-speaker representations derived from enrollment speech, allowing detection of whether a speaker is active even when that speaker is not visually observed. ROAM-ASD-C achieves state-of-the-art performance across five ASD benchmarks: 96.8% mAP on AVA, 98.9% on WASD, 88.8% on UniTalk, 98.7% on Talkies, and 99.5% on ASW. It also improves ROAM-ASD by up to 13.3 mAP under 75% target-track visual removal.

papers.title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising
papers.abstract: Low-count imaging arises when limited illumination or dose yields only a few detected particles in microscopy, such as photons or electrons, causing measurements to be dominated by signal-dependent Poisson shot noise. Supervised denoisers typically require paired clean and noisy observations, whereas many self-supervised approaches exploit spatial or temporal redundancy without directly estimating the underlying particle-arrival process. We introduce PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework based on particle-arrival-rate matching. By modeling particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process, PARM identifies the conditional particle-arrival-rate field with the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. Poisson thinning then splits each observation into complementary lower-exposure views that provide self-supervised rate targets for one another. In implementation, the network estimates the normalized spatial allocation of the conditional rate, while the observed total count determines its global particle mass. Experiments on synthetic data, natural-video sequences corrupted with Poisson noise, and real low-dose electron microscopy demonstrate leading or competitive performance while effectively preserving fine structures. PARM therefore provides a statistically grounded approach to low-count image denoising when clean references are unavailable.

papers.title: Cross-View and Cross-Time Tracking of Crack Evolution in Concrete
papers.abstract: Crack propagation provides richer information than static crack observations for evaluating structural conditions of concrete infrastructure and planning maintenance strategies. Unlike static crack detection, which can now be largely automated using computer vision, vision-based crack tracking is a coupled cross-view and cross-time problem: the same physical crack must retain its identity as camera viewpoints change, while newly developed growth must be distinguished from existing crack segments in a unified reference view. Existing segmentation and 3D reconstruction methods can recover crack masks or scene geometry, but they do not preserve crack identity across views or quantify temporal extension. To address this gap, this study formulates crack growth monitoring as a cross-view and cross-time crack-instance tracking task and proposes a geometry-assisted, morphology-aware framework. The framework first uses image-based geometric registration to align observations from different viewpoints into a shared structural reference, then applies morphology-aware instantiation to assign physically interpretable crack identities, and finally performs temporal mapping in the unified view to distinguish newly developed growth from existing crack segments. To enable evaluation, a temporally annotated dataset was established and used, covering three representative cracking scenarios: single dominant crack propagation, mixed-mode branching, and multiple-crack interaction, with pixel-level masks and cross-time instance labels. Experimental results show that the proposed framework can establish loose cross-view identity correspondence under changing viewpoints, while strict spatial overlap and growth localization remain limited by early micro-crack segmentability and projection drift, highlighting directions for future crack-monitoring research.

papers.title: Semantic-Guided Frequency Modulation for Learned Image Compression
papers.abstract: High-frequency attenuation can reduce the rate of learned image codecs but also remove object boundaries and fine detail. We propose Semantic-Guided Adaptive Latent-Frequency Modulation (SG-AFM), which uses a semantic structural prior to guide attenuation of encoder latents. SG-AFM applies a Haar wavelet transform and combines a fixed semantic-frequency multiplier with a bounded learned correction to modulate high-frequency subbands. The semantic prior is computed only at the encoder. No semantic map is transmitted, and no decoder modules are added. Across six datasets, SG-AFM reduces PSNR-based BD-rate relative to TCM by an average of 13.17%. It achieves the best BD-rate among the compared methods on ExDark, NightCity, and OnePlus, with a mean reduction of 16.80%. An ablation on OnePlus demonstrates the benefit of spatially aligned semantic guidance, and visual comparisons illustrate improved reconstruction of local structures.

papers.title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

papers.title: Accuracy and efficiency of compact foundation models for surface-water mapping during floods
papers.abstract: Pretrained Earth observation models may reduce the effort needed to map surface water, but their value depends on the alternative against which they are compared. We evaluated Prithvi-EO-2.0-Tiny using the 446 hand-labeled Sentinel-2 chips from 11 flood events in Sen1Floods11. A fine-tuned model, a frozen-encoder model, and an identical randomly initialized architecture were compared with a similarly sized U-Net, a larger Prithvi model, and spectral-index thresholds. Experiments varied the number of training chips, excluded events from model fitting, and measured computational cost and prediction reliability. With 252 training chips, U-Net achieved a water intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.856 on the official test set, compared with 0.833 for fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny. Pretraining improved the tiny transformer over random initialization by a reported 0.046 IoU with 25 training chips and 0.023 with 252 chips, but did not reverse the U-Net ranking. Across 11 event-exclusion evaluations, mean IoU was 0.768 for fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny and 0.777 for U-Net; the paired interval included zero. Fine-tuned Prithvi-Tiny processed a 512x512-pixel chip in 16.1 ms on a GPU and 258 ms on a laptop CPU, compared with 30.6 and 665 ms for U-Net. Errors were concentrated near water boundaries, and high predictive entropy identified many, but not all, erroneous pixels. These results support a specific role for compact pretrained models: lower measured computational demand with competitive accuracy, rather than consistent superiority. Event-dependent performance, shared hyperparameter selection, and the distinction between observed water and newly inundated land delimit the conclusions.

papers.title: MedVTok: A General-Purpose Medical Visual Tokenizer
papers.abstract: Multimodal medical AI requires a common visual interface for encoding heterogeneous imaging evidence for patient condition modeling. However, existing medical visual tokenizers are often tied to a specific dimension and imaging modality, forcing multimodal systems to rely on fragmented and poorly reusable representations. We introduce MedVTok, a general-purpose visual tokenizer that maps 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse imaging modalities into a unified token space. Building such a tokenizer poses two key challenges: preserving anatomical structure across dimensions and capturing clinical semantics across modalities. To this end, MedVTok introduces (i) slice differential regularization, which explicitly models inter-slice anatomical coherence missing in previous per-pixel/per-voxel supervision, and (ii) multi-expert representation alignment, which integrates knowledge from multiple medical expert encoders while retaining modality-specific complementary knowledge. Trained on 28M images and 70K volumes across 9 imaging modalities, MedVTok supports classification, retrieval, segmentation, synthesis, visual question answering, and medical report generation through a single tokenizer. Across 24 benchmarks, MedVTok achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating a scalable token interface that unifies medical image dimension, modality, and task usage.

papers.title: Align, Then Adapt: Few-Shot fMRI Visual Reconstruction For New Subjects
papers.abstract: Reconstructing visual images from fMRI data is a central but challenging problem in neuroscience. Despite recent progress, current methods fall short when data and computation are limited-precisely the conditions under which this task is most critical. We introduce Adapter Alignment, a staged, architecture-agnostic training procedure for adapting a pre-trained reconstruction model to a new subject with little data. Rather than letting a shared representation space emerge implicitly, lightweight subject-specific adapters are first explicitly aligned to a pre-trained reference subject on a small set of shared calibration images, and the full pipeline is then fine-tuned while preserving this alignment. The resulting representations not only place different subjects in a shared space but also align them semantically. Our results demonstrate significant gains in low-data regimes, improving reconstruction metrics by up to 8%, and pre-diffusion retrieval shows that these gains reflect additional image-specific information in the fMRI embeddings rather than the generative prior. We also propose a coverage-based algorithm to select representative calibration images. Using both techniques together, we surpass baseline models fine-tuned with one hour of data using only 24 minutes of subject-specific data. The procedure is effective across architectures, reference subjects, and datasets, including adapting 3T subjects to a 7T reference.

papers.title: FermatSyn: SAM2-Enhanced Bidirectional Mamba with Isotropic Spiral Scanning for Multi-Modal Medical Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: Multi-modal medical image synthesis is pivotal for alleviating clinical data scarcity, yet existing methods fail to reconcile global anatomical consistency with high-fidelity local detail. We propose FermatSyn, which addresses three persistent limitations: (1) SAM2-based Prior Encoder that injects domain-aware anatomical knowledge via LoRA$^{+}$ efficient fine-tuning of a frozen SAM2 Vision Transformer; (2) Hierarchical Residual Downsampling Module (HRDM) coupled with a Cross-scale Integration Network (CIN) that preserves high-frequency lesion details and adaptively fuses global--local representations; and (3) continuity constrained Fermat Spiral Scanning strategy within a Bidirectional Fermat Scan Mamba (BFS-Mamba), constructing an approximately isotropic receptive field that substantially reduces the directional bias of raster or spiral serialization. Experiments on SynthRAD2023, BraTS2019, BraTS-MEN, and BraTS-MET show FermatSyn surpasses state-of-the-art methods in PSNR, SSIM, FID, and 3D structural consistency. Downstream segmentation on synthesized images yields no significant difference from real-image training ($p{>}0.05$), confirming clinical utility. Code is available at https://github.com/exsinger-hub/ FermatSyn.

papers.title: Benchmarking Classification Tasks of Chest X-ray AI Across Multinational Public and Private Datasets: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
papers.abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) AI models are increasingly proposed for triage, screening, and rule-out, where the operating point is fixed to miss few abnormalities. Most evaluations instead report threshold-free discrimination on a few public benchmarks, leaving clinically usable performance and generalisability to unseen institutional cohorts poorly characterised. We retrospectively evaluated 10 published CXR classification models on 12 datasets from six countries: seven public benchmarks and five institutional cohorts from China, Japan, and Germany. Models spanned convolutional networks, vision-language models, a question-answering foundation model, and a repurposed encoder. Only image-level classification was assessed; segmentation, detection, and report generation were out of scope. Source labels were harmonised to a common vocabulary. The primary outcome was specificity at 95% sensitivity; PPV at 95% sensitivity and AUROC were secondary outcomes. Estimates weighted each diagnostic task equally, with 95% CIs. MAVL and MedKLIP had the highest overall specificity at 95% sensitivity (0.37 [95% CI 0.31-0.44] and 0.37 [0.30-0.44]) and kept that ranking on tasks evaluable for every model. Their PPV was 0.18 (0.13-0.24) and 0.19 (0.13-0.25): most flagged examinations would be false positives. Specificity was lower on institutional cohorts than on public benchmarks for most models, by 0.13 for MAVL, 0.15 for DenseNet, and 0.09 for MedKLIP. No model was best for every finding, country, lesion extent, or prevalence stratum; specificity fell from 0.34 for diffuse to 0.15 for focal findings. At 95% sensitivity, the best current models clear only about a third of truly negative examinations, and public-benchmark performance overstates what they achieve on unseen institutional data. Operating-point-aware evaluation and external validation on institutional cohorts should precede deployment.

papers.title: Multisource Remote Sensing and Geospatial Analysis of Vineyard Wildfire Impacts and Exposure: The 2019 Kincade Fire
papers.abstract: Working agricultural landscapes are often treated as background to wildfire disasters, even though they are managed fuel mosaics, productive assets, and parts of regional infrastructure systems. We examine vineyard wildfire resilience during the electrically initiated 2019 Kincade Fire in Sonoma County, California, using an open, event-anchored geospatial framework spanning 4,581 vineyard fields (8,813.2 ha), wildland vegetation, surveyed structures, roads, overhead smoke, and post-fire greenness. Sentinel-2, OpenET, gridMET, soils, terrain, NOAA smoke polygons, an ignition-date OpenStreetMap network, and three-dimensional data inventories were analyzed at native decision scales. Vineyard pixels showed substantially lower descriptive dNBR than wildland pixels inside the perimeter (means 0.130 and 0.337). This contrast did not identify a universal vineyard firebreak effect: a segment-clustered boundary model gave a small negative contrast at 100 m (tau = -0.0166) but changed across bandwidths, failed slope continuity, disappeared in a 100 m donut, and produced a wrong-signed placebo. A 250 m spatial GAM reversed the unconditional pattern: after conditioning on location, terrain, and water use, vineyard fraction was positively associated with dNBR, while residual Moran's I remained 0.519. Beyond spectral impact, all mapped vineyards intersected overhead smoke on at least one day (mean 7.78 potential smoke-days per field), 34.2% of road-network nodes were dead ends, and inside-perimeter vineyards showed a larger greenness deficit through 2021 (recovery ratios 0.815 inside and 0.854 outside). Lower immediate spectral impact therefore did not imply complete resilience. The study provides a reproducible urban-rural informatics template separating descriptive contrasts, conditional associations, exposure indicators, and recovery evidence for decisions in working landscapes.

papers.title: A Sentinel-2 benchmark dataset for deep-learning active-fire segmentation across 25 California wildfires, July 2020-August 2026
papers.abstract: This article describes an open image dataset for developing and evaluating active-fire segmentation methods in satellite imagery. The dataset contains 2,148 image-mask pairs from 25 California wildfires, with acquisitions spanning July 2020 to August 2026. Each image is a 512x512-pixel, three-channel composite derived from Sentinel-2 Level-2A bands B12, B11 and B8A at 20 m spatial sampling. A fixed linear rendering is applied throughout the dataset. Corresponding masks distinguish background, SWIR-rule active fire and invalid observations. The masks were generated from shortwave-infrared brightness and near-infrared contrast, followed by constrained neighborhood growth. The release includes chip-level metadata and an incident-disjoint partition containing 18 training, three validation and four test fires. Among the image pairs, 841 contain active-fire labels; these labels occupy 0.0766% of all grid cells. A mask-blind analyst review covers 233 test chips and provides a separate assessment of the rule-generated labels at chip and connected-component levels. Reference training and evaluation code accompanies the data, including a ResNet-34 U-Net implementation with validation-based checkpoint and threshold selection. The archived images, masks, metadata and review annotations support research on rare-class segmentation, learning from algorithmic labels and transfer across fire incidents. The versioned dataset is deposited on Zenodo, with preparation and reuse software maintained in a public GitHub repository.

papers.title: IAR: An Interaction-Aware Approach to Post-Seek Recovery in Adaptive HLS Streaming
papers.abstract: After an unbuffered seek, an adaptive bitrate (ABR) player has little forward buffer at the new position, while its controller may retain a bandwidth estimate from earlier downloads. An expensive first request can delay resumption; later requests may interrupt playback while the buffer rebuilds. We introduce Interaction-Aware Recovery (IAR), a temporary layer around the hls.js ABR controller. After an unbuffered seek, IAR discounts the inherited estimate ({\gamma}=0.15) to set a representation ceiling. Normal adaptation continues below it until 8 s of forward buffer has been rebuilt. In a 200-run paired study spanning four network profiles, ten seek positions, and five strategies, a conservative first request reduced resume delay by a paired median of 2.008 s relative to standard hls.js. Keeping a low ceiling through recovery reduced later interruption under stronger degradation but lowered early presented bitrate. IAR and Fixed-Low-Recovery both used L0 in this campaign, so the results did not show an additional benefit from deriving the ceiling from inherited bandwidth. In 60 additional runs under a fixed Moderate profile, we reset the estimator to six controlled scalar priors. IAR's ceiling changed from L0 to L1 and L2 at the predicted thresholds. Resume and recovery times increased at those transitions; presented bitrate varied non-monotonically and was highest at L2. No stalls occurred. These reset-created priors do not reproduce complete, naturally evolved exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) histories. The results show the benefits and presented-quality costs of conservative post-seek recovery, without establishing an advantage for a history-derived ceiling over a fixed low ceiling.

papers.title: Explainable GeoAI for urban wildfire structure loss: vegetation and built environment in the 2025 Palisades Fire
papers.abstract: Urban wildfire resilience depends on interactions among built form, vegetation condition, and extreme fire weather, yet city-scale risk models often overlook whether predictive skill transfers across neighborhoods. We developed a spatially validated GeoAI workflow for the January 2025 Palisades Fire, linking 12,081 CAL FIRE damage inspections to pre-fire Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, Landsat surface temperature, LANDFIRE fuels, terrain, and OpenStreetMap buildings and roads. Among 9,883 inspected residential structures, 5,566 were destroyed. Random cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC 0.92 for the integrated XGBoost model, but 1 km spatial block validation reduced performance to 0.75; logistic regression performed similarly and was better calibrated. Building count within 100 m was the strongest predictor, with destruction odds increasing 4.12-fold per standard deviation. Vegetation moisture and greenness showed opposing conditional associations: NDMI at 100-300 m was protective (OR 0.52), whereas NDVI at 30-100 m was positively associated with destruction after accounting for moisture (OR 1.74). Predictive information was concentrated at the 100-300 m neighborhood scale. A separate post-fire track mapped burn severity and vegetation recovery without leakage. The results support neighborhood-scale susceptibility screening, moisture-aware vegetation management, and spatial block validation as a minimum standard for single-event urban wildfire modeling.

papers.title: Discrete cosine-sine transform and fast 16-point integer cosine-sine transform low-complexity for video coding
papers.abstract: A matrix method for constructing a discrete cosine-sine transform of order N is proposed, upon which discrete and integer cosine-sine transforms of order 16 are constructed. A fast algorithm for computing an integer cosine-sine transform of order-16 with low multiplicative complexity, which is 8.25 times smaller and requires 115% more addition operations compared to the fast discrete cosine-sine transform algorithm, is presented.

papers.title: TeQCo: Temporal Quota Consistency for Training-Free Video Token Compression
papers.abstract: Video token compression must control both temporal coverage and task relevance, but sequential stages can conflict: a content-driven allocation stage may be overwritten by a global ranking that removes entire temporal positions. We identify this as an allocation conflict and propose TeQCo, a training-free framework that resolves it through temporal quota consistency. TeQCo allocates candidate capacity from first-order changes in normalized frame representations and aggregates all tokens within each frame into a compact candidate set. Candidates are then scored by prior-corrected task attention and selected within integer frame quotas inherited from the first-stage counts. Content variation determines temporal capacity; question relevance determines which candidates fill it. This design guarantees an exact token budget and a per-frame coverage floor whenever feasible. On the 2,700-question Video-MME benchmark with Qwen3-VL-8B, TeQCo achieves 68.52% accuracy at 510 ms TTFT, a 32.9% TTFT reduction with a 1.00-percentage-point accuracy decrease.

papers.title: ContextTom: Training-Free Video VLM Acceleration with Early Spatial Context
papers.abstract: Video vision-language models process thousands of visual tokens before producing an answer. Reducing these tokens early saves computation, but also determines which evidence reaches the language model. We introduce ContextTom, a training-free framework that separates the timing of temporal and spatial compression. Its central idea is to compress time before vision encoding while preserving spatial coverage through early multimodal processing. A fixed-budget temporal partition produces representative medoid anchors, supplemented with bounded local detail from neighboring observations. The anchors retain their complete spatial grids through a short decoder prefix, allowing question tokens to access the visual evidence and completing Qwen3-VL's multi-level visual injections. ContextTom then selects spatial representatives using query attention and agreement across visual feature levels, and continues directly from their computed states. This schedule reduces vision computation and later decoder workload while reusing the prefix. On Qwen3-VL-8B, ContextTom achieves 76.22% accuracy on Video-MME Short with a mean time-to-first-token (TTFT) of 123.5 ms, yielding a 2.77x speedup over full-input inference. It matches the full-input accuracy of 72.20% on EgoSchema with a 2.82x speedup and achieves a 5.54x speedup on LongVideoBench at 59.24% accuracy.

papers.title: Simulated transcranial ultrasound of human language cortex: verifying heard speech needs far less data and signal than decoding it
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound could image cortical blood volume through the temporal bone, but the skull leaves a weak signal, and task-evoked cortical imaging through the intact adult skull has not yet been shown. We built a voxel-specific Monte Carlo link-budget simulation of a probe on the left temple and used it to degrade public fMRI of three people who heard 15 hours of stories. On the same anatomical voxels we trained a published state-of-the-art fMRI language decoder (Tang et al., 2023) and two verifiers that only check a candidate text. In clean data the verifiers needed far less training (11 to 12 minutes against 3.2 to 6.6 hours), but all three learned at a similar rate. Noise changed this qualitatively: the verifiers kept gaining evidence while the decoder slowed and, under simulated transcranial physics, stalled, whereas the verifiers still reached their goal under a favorable simulated link budget. This asymmetry suggests that low-SNR modalities such as transcranial ultrasound may support verification well before decoding.

papers.title: Fully-Automated Multi-Modal Registration of Timelapse Zebrafish OCT+LS Images
papers.abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and light sheet (LS) fluorescence microscopy provide complementary views of tissue morphology and molecular expression, offering a powerful approach for studying embryonic development. However, longitudinal integration of OCT+LS images is challenging because the modalities differ substantially in contrast, spatial resolution, field of view, and visible anatomical features, while embryo growth and movement introduce additional misalignment over time. These challenges stem from both the scale and multimodal nature of the OCT and LS image stacks. We present a fully automated three-dimensional rigid registration framework for aligning OCT and LS volumes of developing zebrafish embryos acquired from 21 to 48 hours post fertilization (HPF). The method does not require pre-existing segmentations or cross-modal feature correspondences, which are often unreliable because OCT and LS capture fundamentally different tissue properties. Registration performance was evaluated across developmental time points using mean target registration error (mTRE) and compared across multiple similarity metrics and optimization methods. Normalized cross-correlation combined with particle swarm optimization produced the most accurate and consistent registration, achieving the lowest mTRE at every evaluated time point compared with the alternative methods. The registration establishes spatial correspondence between OCT tissue morphology and LS fluorescence signals throughout development, enabling integrated longitudinal analysis of structural and molecular changes in living embryos.

papers.title: Complex Domain Inverse Problem Formulation for 4D Flow MRI Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging measures blood velocity fields in three dimensions throughout the cardiac cycle and is increasingly used to assess hemodynamics. However, these measurements are limited by low signal-to-noise ratios and limited spatial resolution, which can compromise their accuracy and reliability. To address these limitations, we investigate the feasibility of spatial resolution enhancement through a complex-domain inverse problem formulation inspired by MRI acquisition principles. Three inversion methods are evaluated: a closed-form approach (FSR), a Plug-and-Play alternating direction method of multipliers (PnP-ADMM), and a pretrained network that takes the forward operator as input (RAM). On simulated data, all three methods outperform 4DFlowNet at x2 and x4 super-resolution factors. On aortic phantom data at x2 super-resolution, PnP-ADMM and RAM achieve lower root-mean-square error than 4DFlowNet in almost all cases. These results highlight the potential of the proposed formulation and support further development and validation.

papers.title: Cascaded Posterior Sampling With Diffusion Priors for highly Accelerated MRI
papers.abstract: Diffusion models are powerful priors for inverse problems, including accelerated MRI. However, modeling the distribution of high-resolution images requires large networks with high computational cost. We propose a posterior sampling framework that uses cascaded diffusion models as multiscale priors. Conditioned on a coarse image, the distribution of fine-scale detail is local and well conditioned, and it can therefore be captured by a small network. Similarly, a small unconditional network is sufficient to represent low-resolution images, and it is used to recover the coarse image from the k-space center. This estimate then conditions the high-resolution prior, which is combined with all measurements to recover the final image. Both priors are trained on images alone, so they apply to any sampling pattern, and data consistency remains linear at every scale. In multi-coil brain MRI, the proposed method improves on the best single-scale diffusion baseline by 4-6 dB in PSNR at 15x acceleration, while each of its separately trained networks is about 10x smaller. The gain grows as the problem becomes more ill-posed, and ablations show that it arises from informative low-resolution conditioning.

papers.title: Semantic-Aware Deformable Feature Alignment for Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of thyroid nodules in ultrasound images is essential for clinical diagnosis yet remains challenging due to boundary ambiguity, speckle noise, and complex geometric variability. Existing methods often fail to reconcile global semantic understanding with precise local boundary delineation, leading to errors in irregular cases. To address this, we propose SDFA-Net, a framework built on semantic-aware deformable feature alignment that explicitly decouples the learning of robust global semantics and detailed local geometry. Our approach integrates three main components: a clustered linear context aggregation module for efficient long-range dependency modeling, an affinity-driven token modulation mechanism using dynamic prototypes to suppress background interference, and a cascaded spatially-aligned feature fusion strategy that achieves sub-pixel geometric alignment across multiple resolution stages. By filtering and aligning multi-scale features, SDFA-Net ensures robust fusion that is both semantically meaningful and geometrically accurate. We validate our method through extensive experiments on three public thyroid ultrasound datasets, TN3K, TUCC, and DDTI, where it demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework offers a generalizable solution for precise medical image segmentation in boundary-ambiguous scenarios.
